ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account action against the driver — his forgotten "I'm Here" tap is a single non-fraudulent omission on a clean 951-trip record.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the driver, who alleges a rider no-show, so the fee enters through NS-0's "driver cancelled, alleges no-show" branch and stands or falls on NS-1 alone [F4][NS-0]. The trace settles NS-1(i) as failed: no arrival confirmation of any kind is on record — no "I'm Here" tap and no platform automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null) [F5][F6][NS-1]. Because (i) fails, N-1's conjunctive test cannot be met, and NS-1 is not satisfied no matter how strong the geographic evidence is [F1][F2][F3][NS-1]. NS-2 then applies on its plain terms: where any of (i)(ii)(iii) is unmet, the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full [F7][NS-2]. The amount is fixed by the fare record, not by any computation: the cancellation fee charged is $6.61 [F4][F7], and the trace fixes the amount at $6.61, so refund_full is the outcome.

The platform's logged arrival time of 22:41:30 and the 5 min 20 s inside 200 m are real but cannot supply (i) [F2][F5][NS-1]: NS-1(ii) requires the driver to have been within 200 m at the moment of the arrival confirmation, and the trace marks (ii) and (iii) as failed precisely because there was no such confirmation (0 s measured after a non-existent tap) [F6][NS-1]. The driver concedes the omission in his own statement — "I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there" — but a driver's statement is a claim, not the platform confirmation the clause requires [F12][NS-1]. The chat does not cure it either: the driver's own messages at 22:43 and 22:46 place him at the pickup and announce the cancellation, but they are not an arrival confirmation, and the complete timestamped record shows no rider reply [F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

The rider's "I was on my way down" is a statement unsupported by any gps or timeline fact, and the 9 min 50 s from acceptance to cancellation with silence in the chat does show a rider who did not appear [F4][F11][NS-4]. But NS-4 is about rider-initiated cancellation and no rule lets a driver's defective no-show flow stand on substance alone; the rider's remedy for a fee she considers unfair is the NS-7 human appeal, and this ruling recommends the same voucher remedy [F7][NS-7].

NS-2's account action is not triggered: the flag condition is a driver who pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him away from the pickup, and no such fake confirmation exists here — the tap never happened [F6][F1][NS-2]. Nor is RD-6 engaged: the breach is a single forgotten tap, and the driver's 90-day record shows 951 trips with zero upheld disputes, so the "repeated" threshold (≥1 prior upheld route dispute) is not met [F16][F17][RD-6]. Profiles are context only and decide nothing [F16][F17][RD-6].

SAFE-1 screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's written statement and the rider's complaint. They contain a pickup identification, a wait-and-cancel notice and an assertion of being on the way down — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any direction, so no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation arises [F9][F10][F12][NS-7]. Evidence is sufficient: the settlement elements (who cancelled, the arrival confirmation, the fee charged, the chat timing) are each on the record, so no gap remains [F4][F6][F7][F11].

rejected_claims.reason: The 5 min 20 s within 200 m and the platform's 22:41:30 arrival stamp speak only to NS-1(ii)/(iii), and the trace records (ii) and (iii) as failed because there was no arrival confirmation at which to measure them; NS-1 requires (i)(ii)(iii) together and (i) is failed on F6 [F2][F5][F6][NS-1].

The complete, timestamped chat shows the rider sent nothing, but rider silence is not itself a no-show finding under NS-1; the driver's own messages (F9, F10) are his characterisation of being at the pickup, not the platform arrival confirmation NS-1(i) requires [F9][F10][F11][F6][NS-1].

The $6.61 and the 1.0× surge are not in dispute; whether the fee is valid is exactly what NS-0 routes through NS-1, and with NS-1(i) failed the fee does not stand and NS-2 requires refund_full [F4][F7][F8][F6][NS-0][NS-1][NS-2].

There is no fact recording any $4.50 earned by the driver — the only sum on record is the $6.61 charged to the rider (F7) — and profile facts such as F16/F17 can never alone decide a case [F7][F16][F17][NS-1].

Accepted only as far as it goes: proximity of 34 m and a 4 min stationary stop 40 m away (F1, F3) is not one of NS-1's three conditions, and being nearby cannot substitute for the missing arrival confirmation [F1][F3][F6][NS-1].
